title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a Grothendieck manuscript page. It is a typescript page, scanned upside down, of a Bourbaki draft: rédaction n° 382, page 83. It belongs to the material on differentiable and analytic manifolds (the 'Variétés différentielles et analytiques' project), §7.2 on jets and bundles of principal parts. Grothendieck evidently used the back of discarded Bourbaki drafts as scrap paper. The neighbouring pages, his handwritten crystal and Dieudonné-module computations, are presumably on the other side or on adjacent sheets.

The mathematics is as follows.

(i) End of 7.2.3. The germs at x of sections of a vector bundle E having contact of order ≥ k' with the zero section form the fibre of a vector subbundle of P^k(X,E). This subbundle is a module over the algebra bundle P^k(X). In particular ker(P^k(X,E) → P^{k-1}(X,E)) ≅ S^k(T(X)^*) ⊗ E.

(ii) 7.2.4. Take a submersion π: Y → X of C^r manifolds and k' ≤ k ≤ r, with ℓ = k − k'. The canonical map J^k(X,Y) → J^ℓ(X, J^{k'}(X,Y)) of 7.1.10 induces a C^{r−k} map P^k(X,π) → P^ℓ(X,π_1), where π_1 is the projection of P^{k'}(X,π). When the base field K has characteristic 0, this map is an isomorphism onto a submanifold. This is the embedding of higher jets into iterated (holonomic) jets.

(iii) 7.2.5. Functoriality of P^k with respect to morphisms of submersions over X, i.e. a map g with π'∘g = π. Exactness of P^k(X,−) on exact sequences of vector bundles. The isomorphism P^k_x(X, A⊗B) ≅ P^k_x(X,A) ⊗_{P^k_x(X)} P^k_x(X,B).

(iv) 7.2.6 begins base change. Given f: X → X' and Y = X ×_{X'} Y', the map j^k(f, Id) induces a map of principal-part bundles; the page breaks off mid-sentence.

This is standard textbook material on jet bundles. Its role is foundational exposition for Bourbaki, not a research problem of Grothendieck's.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The characteristic-0 hypothesis in 7.2.4 is appropriate: Bourbaki's setting allows complete ultrametric fields, where in characteristic p the iterated-jet map need not be injective because of factorials in Taylor coefficients.
Exactness in 7.2.5 implicitly requires the sequence of bundles to be exact with locally constant ranks (the usual Bourbaki convention).

missed.claim: Archival and historical detail only. Grothendieck's crystal notes of around 1970 were written on the backs of Bourbaki draft n° 382 on jets and principal parts. This helps date and place the Bourbaki manuscripts circulating in his hands. There is no mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: n° 382 - 83 - ... 7.2.4. Soient X, Y des variétés de classe C^r
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Useful for historians of Bourbaki's Variétés drafts and for reconstructing the physical order of cote 8. It does not bear on the mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Bourbaki typescript on jet bundles, reused as scrap paper. It contains standard results and none of Grothendieck's own research content.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (n° 382, p. 83), not Grothendieck's handwriting, except for the handwritten footnote and the margin numbers.
The handwritten footnote (1) fills the gap in 7.2.5. It should read: '... tel que π'∘g = π, et k un entier ≤ r. L'application j^k(Id, g) (cf. n° 7.1.11) induit une application P^k(g) ...'.
In 7.2.6 the blank '(        )' is a lacuna left in the typescript; it is presumably meant for a similar insertion (likely the hypothesis on k).
